statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail firms to 24%, the top of the watch band and still one point below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold. NQ has extended to a fresh overnight high and sits within five points of it, which is a genuine amplifier, but the move is a thin-liquidity Globex grind that has not yet met a liquid two-way session, and the long end of the Treasury curve has not confirmed it. The concentrated event risk falls in the narrow 12:00-15:00Z window spanning US jobless claims, a Fed appearance, the cash open and ISM manufacturing.
headline: NQ extends to 31,024.75 and holds the high as Micron lifts the Nikkei 2.8%, while a 5.62% 30-year yield withholds confirmation
body: December E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures trade 31,020.25, up 321.50 points or 1.05% from the 30,698.75 settle, after printing a fresh overnight high at 31,024.75 and holding within 4.50 points of it. The Globex path has been close to one-way: the session low is 30,684.50, the full range spans 340.25 points or 1.11%, and there has been no observed retracement test of the reclaimed 30,812.75 shelf. Turnover remains thin at 53.53k contracts, and the 31,094.75 pivot that would mark genuine uptrend resumption is still roughly 74 points above. The driver is identifiable and has broadened since the preceding hour: Micron's record fiscal fourth quarter and its 61.5 billion dollar first-quarter revenue guidance, together with long-term supply agreements rising to 32 billion dollars from 22 billion in June, lifted Japan's Nikkei 225 by 2.8% to 68,606.81 with Lasertec up 10.80%, Taiyo Yuden up 8.64%, Murata up 8.10%, Advantest up 7.27%, TDK up 6.14%, Kioxia up 5.72% and Tokyo Electron up 5.71%, while the Kospi added 1.2% and Alphabet gained 1.5% on its Gemini 4 Argon announcement. Against that, the completed cash session argues reversion is intact: NDX closed 30,408.50, the exact low of a 30,408.50 to 30,630.45 range, a full intraday fade of a 0.23% gain. Cross-assets still do not confirm an equity melt-up. The 2-year eased to 4.89% and the 10-year to 5.28%, both only marginally lower, while the 30-year steadied at 5.62% after reaching its highest level since 2002, and that refusal of the long end to retreat is the same mechanism that faded an overnight risk-asset pop. WTI fell 1.68% to 88.90 dollars and Brent 1.36% to 96.70 dollars, and the VIX closed at 16.34, up 1.87% but still low. August core PCE at 0.2% monthly and 3.0% annually against a 3.3% forecast, with headline at 3.4% against 3.7%, has cut October Fed hike odds to roughly 35% from about 50% the prior day, which supports the equity bid without resolving the curve. Two amplifiers are now observed: repeated extension to fresh overnight highs with price held at the extreme, and aligned Asian semiconductor participation. They are offset by thin pre-event liquidity, an unconfirmed long end, falling oil, a subdued VIX and a completed cash session that mean-reverted in full. Tail therefore firms one point to 24%, remaining inside the watch band, with an upgrade reserved for observed continuation in a liquid session. Shared Finviz context was collected 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial status, so at roughly 30 hours old it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used; this assessment rests entirely on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail sat at 15-16% through the European and early US hours of 30 September with the mode mixed, stepped into the watch band at 20% from 12:00Z as the US data block and the long-end selloff developed, and peaked at 23% around 15:00-16:00Z. It held a 20-22% range through the US afternoon and the Asian session, then firmed from 21% at 02:00Z to 22% and 23% as NQ began printing successive fresh overnight highs. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 65% and 72%, and Confidence held 85-88%.
outlookSummary: The mapped danger window is 12:00-15:00Z, covering initial and continuing jobless claims at 12:30Z, Fed's Barkin at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z. Forecast Tail stays inside the watch band across all 24 slots, holding 24% through the late Asian hours on the assumption that the overnight bid persists untested, easing to 23% from the European open where two-way liquidity would normally produce a measurable retracement, returning to 24% across the event hours where Stress peaks at 76%, then decaying to 21-22% through the US afternoon, the cash close and the Asian session. Treating the event stack as a checkpoint rather than an automatic block follows the observed pattern that release importance and surprise magnitude primarily raise Stress and whipsaw risk. Attention then rotates to the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October, which falls outside this forecast window. An upward Tail reassessment would require observed persistent one-way structure in a liquid session: shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension after a failed pullback, acceptance above the 31,094.75 pivot, NQ holding a session extreme through the US cash open, or the long end of the curve realigning behind the move.
